applies_to: roof and wall framing concept review
applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: UK/Eurocode-oriented portal-frame guidance. Concept guidance only.

claims.text: Portal-frame roof plan bracing can provide a stiff anchorage for purlins that restrain rafters.
Side rails and cladding can rely on a braced side-wall framework, and that framework can help stabilize columns when represented correctly.
Secondary members should be represented with their restraint role and load-transfer role separated, because a purlin or girt may do one, both, or neither for a given check.

limitations: This card does not prove that a purlin, side rail, cladding system, or stay can provide the restraint required by a design check.
Manufacturer data and project-specific connection details may be required before assigning restraint stiffness.

pages_used: Portal frames: Vertical bracing, Plan bracing, Restraint to inner flanges

summary: Purlins and girts should be modeled as secondary members whose load-transfer and restraint roles are explicit, not assumed from their names alone.
title: Steel Portal Purlins And Girts
